title: Stop the 400 line template error at the door
summary: A trait and a static_assert shorten join, concepts replace them, and one include swap breaks the build.

turns.user: called join with a vector<Point> and got 400 lines of template vomit. no idea where to even look

assistant.body: Point has no output operator. The diagnostic is long because it only fails deep inside ostream. Let's add a trait that answers whether an element is streamable, so the error lands closer to the call site.

turns.user: wire that into a static_assert. i want the type name in the message

assistant.body: The static_assert message is a string literal, so the type name cannot be pasted into it. Naming the element type first gets you the substituted type on the failing line, which is the next best thing.

turns.user: we are on C++20 already. rewrite with concepts? diagnostic should be shorter that way

assistant.body: With a concept the failure is a few lines at the call site. Streamable carries the element requirement and std::ranges::input_range constrains the range itself, so the trait and the static_assert both go away.

turns.user: actually make sep a string_view. every caller passes a literal anyway

assistant.body: The signature is a single source of truth split across the declaration and the definition, so one substitution covers both. string_view owns nothing, so a literal caller also stops building a temporary std::string. Swapping the include as well.
sed -i '' 's/const std::string& sep/std::string_view sep/g; s/#include <string>/#include <string_view>/' src/util/join.h

turns.user: you broke the build. return type is still std::string

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect: the string include had to stay rather than be swapped, because the return type is still std::string. Escaping a newline on the right side of the substitution turns that one line back into two.
